title: How a Network Learns: Loss and Gradient Descent
summary: A neural network is a function with millions of adjustable numbers. Training measures how wrong it is and nudges every number downhill. Every LLM is trained this way.
objectives: Describe a model as a parameterised function and count its parameters
Compute a loss (mean squared error and cross-entropy) by hand
Carry out one step of gradient descent and explain the learning rate
Explain backpropagation as the chain rule applied layer by layer
Explain why hidden layers and non-linear activations are needed (XOR)
prerequisites: No machine-learning background. You should be comfortable multiplying and adding numbers and with the idea of a function: numbers in, a number out. A little calculus (what a slope is) helps but is explained as we go.
